title: Applied AI - Member of Technical Staff
description: About UsWe’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.About The RoleApplied AI Research at Callosum discovers the methods that make real AI workloads faster, cheaper and better, and turns them into systems that run in production. You will study how agentic workflows, retrieval pipelines and code intelligence stacks actually behave, then invent ways to optimise them at a systems level.A single optimisation can touch agent and workflow design, context and prompting, model choice, the serving stack and the silicon underneath. So we don't hire specialists in one layer. We hire researchers who can reason across the whole system, from agentic design down to the specifics of the model, and who have a feel for how inference and hardware shape what is possible.The role is research-led and engineering-heavy. You will need first-principles judgment to see what kind of system a problem needs, the rigour to prove that it works, and the engineering skill to build it yourself.You will sit across our research and platform functions. What you discover becomes product capability, and what you see in real workloads sets the research agenda. We run a flat Member of Technical Staff structure. Responsibility and scope grow with what you demonstrate, including leadership of the Applied AI Research function as the team scales.What You'll Work OnOur research tries to construct optimal inference systems from the silicon layer all the way up to the harness: the system will learn from the actual deployment profile and tasks it is used on and optimise itself. Open problems you will own include:⁠ ⁠Reverse-engineering agentic systems. Infer the structure of agentic systems from minimal data, and find where it spends compute it doesn't need to.⁠ ⁠Routing. Build robust routers that send each request to the cheapest or fastest path that strictly matches or beats the incumbent model on quality.⁠ ⁠Proving there is no regression. Design layered proxy evaluations, that bound quality ever more tightly, from coarse checks down to a granular understanding of the system.⁠ ⁠New optimisation surface area. Extend the same automatic, detection to new optimisation techniques, and help decide which ones we pursue next.⁠ ⁠Research that ships. Run rigorous experiments, write up what you learn, and work with our platform team to turn what works into general product capability.⁠ ⁠Shared research infrastructure. Build the evaluation harnesses, benchmarks and experiment tooling the team runs on.How We Work⁠ ⁠Generalists by design. Our cadence is fast and our priorities move as we learn. You will move between projects as the problem demands, so breadth and the speed at which you learn matter more than depth in one niche.⁠ ⁠Research judged by production. A result counts when it holds on real workloads. Ideas move quickly from hypothesis to experiment to a deployed system.⁠ ⁠Close to real workloads. You work from real production systems and pipelines. Customer contact is scoped: team members who show an aptitude for it can take on more customer-facing technical work, but it is not the core of the role.⁠ ⁠A mix of experience. We hire across seniority levels. Experienced researchers bring proven practice from large-scale AI development, earlier-career members bring speed and fresh eyes, and each learns from the other.What You Bring⁠ ⁠Broad, foundational knowledge across the modern AI stack: agent and workflow design, LLMs and how they work inside, and inference and serving. You can reason about how a change in one layer affects the others.⁠ ⁠Exceptional technical depth, demonstrated through any of: research that shipped, production AI systems at scale, or an early or founding role where you owned the system end to end.⁠ ⁠Rigour in experimental design, evaluation and benchmarking. You can tell a real improvement from noise, and you design the measurement before you trust the result.⁠ ⁠A very fast learner who goes to first principles when the map runs out.⁠ ⁠Strong engineering skills: you build the systems you research.⁠ ⁠A bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and a strong sense of ownership.What Sets You Apart⁠ ⁠An early or founding role at an AI-first, deep-tech company, where you made key technical decisions from first principles.⁠ ⁠You have designed and built multi-agent or agentic systems from the ground up, and you also have depth lower in the stack.⁠ ⁠Low-level systems or performance engineering: kernels, serving engines or latency-critical systems.⁠ ⁠Experience of large-scale AI development at a frontier lab or big tech company, and the engineering practices that come with it.⁠ ⁠Research in inference optimisation, model internals, evaluation, routing or distillation.⁠ ⁠Publications, open-source work or public write-ups that show how you think.⁠ ⁠Familiarity with novel accelerator platforms.⁠ ⁠Experience working directly with external engineering teams.What We Offer⁠ ⁠Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience⁠ ⁠Equity & Ownership⁠ ⁠Private healthcare⁠ ⁠We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world⁠ ⁠We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell usWe're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all. title: Expert Talent Pool, Agents and RL
description:
About the Role Join an expert network supporting AI human-data projects focused on agents and reinforcement learning. You will help design training environments, evaluation systems, and demonstrations that make agent behavior measurable and reliable, with opportunities matched to projects as they become available. What You'll Do Design reinforcement learning environments, including Python and Docker setups, state spaces, tool integrations, and scoring mechanisms. Build robust verifiers and reward functions that resist agents gaming evaluation criteria. Translate workflows in business software, finance, and operations into scenarios with measurable success criteria. Integrate REST APIs and create test harnesses using tools such as pytest. Lead agent demonstration and computer-use programs, setting quality standards for trace collection. Grade and repair agent trajectories, and guide contributors on evaluation practices. What We're Looking For At least 5 years of experience in software engineering, QA automation, machine learning, reinforcement learning, or business systems and operations paired with hands-on agent or RL data work. Strong Python skills and experience building tools or services that others rely on. Experience designing environments, verifiers, reward functions, or test harnesses to evaluate software or agent behavior, using tools such as pytest, Playwright, Selenium, or Gymnasium-style environments. Hands-on experience with agent or RL data, such as demonstrations, trajectory grading, trace collection, or computer-use demonstrations. Experience with REST APIs and Docker, plus domain expertise modeling workflows in business systems such as CRM or ERP platforms. Experience leading or reviewing data, evaluation, or demonstration work is valuable. A degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field is also relevant. Compensation & Benefits $80 to $200 per hour, depending on project, field, and level. Compensation is based on hours worked. Location Fully remote. Projects typically run from one week to several months. Originally posted on Himalayas
